name: beautiful-rust
description: Write, review, port, and enforce idiomatic Rust: three skills distilled from the Google Rust Style Guide, the Rust API Guidelines, Effective Rust, Rust Design Patterns, and Microsoft's Pragmatic Rust Guidelines, plus a drop-in clippy config.

interface.longDescription:
Three skills for Rust developers, distilled from the Google Rust Style Guide, the Rust API Guidelines, Effective Rust, Rust Design Patterns, and Microsoft's Pragmatic Rust Guidelines.

rust-best-practices guides new Rust code: error handling, API design, ownership, traits, async, unsafe and FFI, tests, and docs. It includes guidance for the Bevy game engine.

rust-review reviews a file, crate, or diff and returns a prioritized report. Every finding cites a file and line, the rule it breaks, and the smallest fix.

rust-port ports C, C++, Python, Go, JavaScript, or TypeScript to idiomatic Rust with the same behavior. It ports the original tests first and writes a PORTING.md that lists every deliberate difference.

The skills contain instructions and reference text only. They make no network calls and collect no data. When a Rust toolchain is available, the skills run cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo test on your project; without one, they work from the code alone. A drop-in clippy config is available in the GitHub repository.
capabilities: Review Rust code with cited rules
Port code to Rust with the same behavior
defaultPrompt: Review this Rust crate and list what to fix first
Port this Python module to idiomatic Rust
Write a Rust function that parses this config format

publication.release_notes: Bevy support, a Claude Code vs Codex benchmark, and every Rust example compiled in CI.
